report_name: Russian APT Star Blizzard Impersonates Hacked Firm to Attack New Target

threat_actors.name: Star Blizzard
threat_actors.description: Russian FSB-linked APT group that weaponized data stolen from a U.S. organization to phish a second U.S. entity. The group is focused on intelligence gathering for the Russian government and targets high-value entities in North America and Europe.
threat_actors.goals: Intelligence gathering for the Russian government.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
attack_patterns.description: Star Blizzard spammed a target's super admin account with MFA push notifications until the user eventually approved one, a technique known as MFA fatigue, to gain initial access to a U.S. organization in late 2025.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure
attack_patterns.description: The group used a residential proxy network to make their login attempts appear geographically close to the victim, thereby evading location-based security alerts.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access to a compromised organization, Star Blizzard performed a bulk download of the victim's entire cloud storage drive.

attack_patterns.name: Gather Victim Identity Information
attack_patterns.description: The attackers exported full employee and contact lists from a compromised organization's domain to identify new targets and craft convincing social engineering lures.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Star Blizzard used a stolen identity and contact information from a previous breach to conduct a highly targeted phishing campaign against a new U.S. organization.

attack_patterns.name: File Deletion
attack_patterns.description: The group accessed the admin console of the compromised organization to erase logs and other evidence of their intrusion.

identities.name: U.S. Organization (Victim 1)
identities.description: A U.S. organization compromised by Star Blizzard in late 2025 via an MFA fatigue attack. Data exfiltrated from this victim was used to target a second organization.

identities.name: U.S. Organization (Victim 2)
identities.description: A U.S. organization targeted in 2026 with a phishing campaign where Star Blizzard impersonated an employee from a previously compromised firm.

identities.name: FSB
identities.description: Russia's Federal Security Service, which is reportedly linked to the Star Blizzard APT group.

identities.name: Google's Threat Intelligence Group
identities.description: The security organization that reported on Star Blizzard's activities.

infrastructure.name: Star Blizzard Residential Proxy Network
infrastructure.description: A residential proxy network used by Star Blizzard to make login attempts appear legitimate and evade location-based security alerts.

indicators.name: Star Blizzard MFA Fatigue Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Star Blizzard MFA Fatigue Attempt
id: 2b8a1c3d-9e4f-4b1a-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects a high number of MFA denial events for a single user in a short period, indicative of an MFA fatigue attack as used by Star Blizzard. This rule detects a single denial and is intended for use in a correlation search.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/russian-apt-poses-as-employee-of-hacked-firm-to-breach-another-us-organization/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-18
tags:
  - attack.t1621
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: '50074' # Interrupt
    Status.failureReason|contains: 'MFA denied; user declined the authentication.'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a high volume of MFA push notifications sent to a single user in a short time frame, which is indicative of an MFA fatigue or push bombing attack as used by Star Blizzard.

indicators.name: Suspicious Bulk Mailbox Export
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Bulk Mailbox Export
id: 8f9b0a1c-2d3e-4f5a-6b7c-8d9e0f1a2b3c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of PowerShell to initiate a mailbox export request, which can be used for bulk data exfiltration from cloud environments like Microsoft 365, a technique observed in the Star Blizzard campaign.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/russian-apt-poses-as-employee-of-hacked-firm-to-breach-another-us-organization/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-18
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.t1114.002
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'New-MailboxExportRequest'
      - '-FilePath'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors for the use of administrative commands or APIs that perform mass downloads or exports from cloud storage, a technique used by Star Blizzard for data exfiltration.
